takes.overview: Best team on paper: #1 in projected strength and 96% playoff odds after the Martone and Granlund adds. D is the edge - #1 in per-game quality (Bouchard, Seider, Clarke, Chychrun) - and goalies rank #1 too; forwards (#3) are where upgrades should go. Hellebuyck is still suspended (latest report Sep 16) and Bedard has no firm timeline per Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times, so both stay flagged, not discounted.
takes.matchup: Week 1 is in hand: up 30-12 on Angie's and projected 131-105 (85%). Starts left are even (46 vs 48), so don't burn adds chasing volume this week - save them for Week 2.
takes.roster: Celebrini, Bouchard and Seider are the core. Zacha, McKenna and Martone are your cheapest cuts by the model; Martone is your upside bet, so if a pickup forces a move, Zacha is the cleaner drop and McKenna the second option.
takes.free_agents: Hartman (+36) and Strome (+27) are the best forward adds - forwards are your weakest group. Watch the opportunity list: Larkin is out short-term (per Max Bultman of The Athletic), which helps Arvidsson for a week or two, not the season.
takes.trades: Tuch remains the sell-high chip: ESPN values him well above your projections. Tuch to Angie's for Matthew Tkachuk + Thomas Harley is the most balanced idea (you +35, them +13) and it adds a D. Keep both healthy goalies while Hellebuyck is suspended.
takes.playoffs: Your playoff weeks (Mar 22-Apr 4) project 1st in the league, but you have about 91 open skater-slot-days and only 4 wasted games - the problem is light days, not crowded ones. Late-season pickups should come from teams that play on your open days; Strome (7 of 8 games on open days) leads the free-agent list.
